hints: Multiply $4\tan x + 3\cos x + \frac{1}{\cos x} = 0$ by $\cos x$ to get $4\sin x + 3\cos^2 x + 1 = 0$.
Replace $\cos^2 x = 1 - \sin^2 x$ and factorise $(3\sin x + 2)(\sin x - 2) = 0$.
walkthrough:
Express $\tan x$ as $\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}$ and multiply the entire equation by $\cos x$:
$$4\left(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\right) + 3\cos x + \frac{1}{\cos x} = 0 \implies 4\sin x + 3\cos^2 x + 1 = 0$$

Replace $\cos^2 x$ with $1 - \sin^2 x$ using the fundamental identity:
$$4\sin x + 3(1 - \sin^2 x) + 1 = 0 \implies 4\sin x + 3 - 3\sin^2 x + 1 = 0$$
$$3\sin^2 x - 4\sin x - 4 = 0$$

Factorise the quadratic equation in $\sin x$:
$$(3\sin x + 2)(\sin x - 2) = 0$$

Reject $\sin x = 2$ (since $|\sin x| \le 1$) to conclude:
$$\sin x = -\frac{2}{3}$$

Use the result from part (i) with the compound argument $(2x - 20^\circ)$:
$$\sin(2x - 20^\circ) = -\frac{2}{3}$$

Determine the corresponding interval for $(2x - 20^\circ)$ given $0^\circ \le x \le 180^\circ$:
$$-20^\circ \le 2x - 20^\circ \le 340^\circ$$

Find the reference angle and locate solutions in the 3rd and 4th quadrants:
$$\alpha = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) \approx 41.81^\circ$$
$$2x - 20^\circ = 180^\circ + 41.81^\circ = 221.81^\circ \implies 2x = 241.81^\circ \implies x \approx 120.9^\circ$$
$$2x - 20^\circ = 360^\circ - 41.81^\circ = 318.19^\circ \implies 2x = 338.19^\circ \implies x \approx 169.1^\circ$$
$$(\text{Solutions: } x = 120.9^\circ, \quad 169.1^\circ)$$
